name: RAFT - Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning (RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG)
venue: COLM 2024 (Conference on Language Modeling); originally arXiv:2403.10131 (cs.CL), submitted 15 Mar 2024, revised 5 Jun 2024
authors_affiliation: Tianjun Zhang, Shishir G. Patil, Naman Jain, Sheng Shen, Matei Zaharia, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez. All from the Department of Computer Science, UC Berkeley.
code_url: https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla (RAFT code and demo open-sourced under the Gorilla project)
task_domain: Domain-specific open-book question answering / knowledge-intensive RAG. Covered domains: biomedical QA (PubMedQA), multi-hop Wikipedia QA (HotpotQA), open-domain QA (Natural Questions, TriviaQA), and code/API-call generation (Gorilla APIBench: HuggingFace, Torch Hub, TensorFlow Hub documentation).
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, supervised post-training (fine-tuning) recipe for the 'domain-specific open-book exam' setting where the test-time document collection / domain is known a priori. The model is trained on (question, retrieved documents -> chain-of-thought answer) tuples and at test time is run in a standard RAG setup with top-k retrieved documents. Supervision: question-answer pairs plus GPT-4-1106-generated chain-of-thought answers; golden vs distractor document labels are available during training data construction. Not interactive, no multi-agent, no test-time learning.
what_is_retrieved: Documents (text passages / API documentation chunks). At training time these are partitioned into 'golden' documents (containing the answer) and 'distractor' documents (irrelevant); at test time they are top-k retriever outputs.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (the fixed in-domain document collection / knowledge base, e.g. PubMed abstracts, Wikipedia, API docs). No agent-written growing memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k retrieval objective at test time (model evaluated with top-k retrieved documents, typically top-3). RAFT does not optimize the retriever or aim for completeness of a minimal set; instead it trains the reader/generator to be robust to a varying number of top-k documents and to ignore distractors, and it studies generalization across different k at train and test time.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; only a Retrieve-then-read pattern is realized, no Reuse/Revise/Retain of cases).
explicit_cbr_grounding: false - The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it is positioned as a retrieval-augmented fine-tuning recipe.
retrieval_unit: document (text passage / API documentation entry). 'Golden' documents contain the answer-relevant span; the model is trained to cite verbatim the right sequence from the relevant document.
index_source: Static, fixed in-domain corpus known a priori. Retrieval store is not induced online or grown at test time; training data is constructed offline by labeling golden vs distractor documents.
index_structure_topology: Flat document corpus / flat vector index (standard RAG retrieval over the domain corpus). No graph or hierarchical organization is introduced by RAFT.
retriever_type: Off-the-shelf / retriever-agnostic. RAFT explicitly states it is independent of the retriever used; experiments use a standard RAG retrieval pipeline (dense retrieval) but RAFT itself does not propose or train a retriever. [uncertain] exact retriever implementation (e.g., specific dense model) for each dataset.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf retriever; RAFT does not train the retriever). The learning signal is applied only to the reader/generator LLM via supervised fine-tuning on golden+distractor contexts with CoT answers.
query_construction: Raw input question is used directly as the retrieval query at test time (no query decomposition, expansion, or rewriting in the base RAFT method).
query_granularity: Task-level (one query per input question, one-shot at the start of answering).
when_to_retrieve: one-shot (single retrieval of top-k documents prepended to the prompt before generation; no iterative or active re-retrieval).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (always retrieve once per question, both at training-data construction and at test time). No confidence/uncertainty/learned-classifier trigger.
reranking: None. No reranking stage is introduced; the model is trained directly to read top-k retrieved documents and ignore distractors.
retrieved_context_refinement: Distractor handling via training (distractor-aware SFT) rather than post-retrieval filtering. The model learns to ignore distractor documents and to cite-then-reason; there is no separate compression/decompose/rerank stage at inference.
tool_document_engineering: For the Gorilla APIBench domains (HuggingFace, Torch Hub, TensorFlow Hub), the retrievable items are API documentation entries used as documents; no special synthetic-query augmentation or instruction-tuned tool embeddings are applied beyond using the raw documentation as golden/distractor docs. [uncertain] finer engineering details.
index_content_separation: N/A - No progressive-disclosure / lightweight-index-then-content separation; full documents are placed directly in context.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A - Static document index; no live tool-store synchronization or MCP/RapidAPI integration. For Gorilla APIBench the model generates API calls but RAFT itself does not maintain a live tool index.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A - No modeling of inter-tool/inter-API dependencies.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation as a training signal: retrieved (golden + distractor) documents are concatenated with the question in the fine-tuning input, and the model is trained (standard SFT, supervised next-token) to produce a chain-of-thought answer that cites verbatim spans from the golden document. At inference, top-k retrieved documents are prepended to the prompt (standard RAG).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-read (one-shot exemplar-free): top-k documents retrieved once and placed in context, then the model reasons (chain-of-thought) and answers. No tree search, MCTS, or hierarchical subtask planning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer (single retrieval feeds a single chain-of-thought reasoning trace that produces one answer). No per-step or per-token re-retrieval.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation; the mechanism is supervised fine-tuning, not CBR-style case revision).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw document text injected into the prompt context. The generated output is a free-text chain-of-thought ('##Reason: ... ##Answer: ...') that quotes verbatim the relevant span from the golden document as citation.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document (verbatim passage / API doc). The injected retrieved unit is unabstracted source text; abstraction happens only in the model's generated CoT answer.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Distractor-aware supervised fine-tuning: training each example with one golden document mixed with distractor documents, plus including (1-P)% of examples with NO golden document (only distractors) to force the model to discern and ignore irrelevant content; combined with cite-then-reason CoT supervision. This trains the reader to be robust to irrelevant retrieved text and to a varying number of top-k documents.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow memory). Knowledge is baked into model weights via fine-tuning on the static domain corpus.
write_back: false - The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into any external memory at deployment; learning is a one-time offline fine-tuning step.
online_growth: false - The retrievable store is the static in-domain corpus; it does not grow during deployment/test time.
write_back_trigger: never - No write-back; the model is frozen after offline fine-tuning and the document store is fixed.
failure_experience_usage: Distractor (negative/irrelevant) documents are used during training as negative context the model must learn to ignore, including (1-P)% of training examples that contain ONLY distractor documents and no golden document. There is no storage/retrieval of failed trajectories or corrective rules; negatives are static distractor docs, not recorded failures.
memory_evolution_update: N/A - No stored memory entries to mutate; the only update is the one-time fine-tuning of model weights.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: false - Retrieval is a fixed similarity top-k from an off-the-shelf retriever; it is not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy. RAFT learns the reader/generator, not a retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A - Single-model, single-agent setting; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: PubMedQA (biomedical QA), HotpotQA (multi-hop Wikipedia QA), Natural Questions (NQ), TriviaQA, and Gorilla APIBench: HuggingFace Hub, Torch Hub, and TensorFlow Hub API-call generation.
benchmark_family: QA (PubMedQA), multi-hop QA (HotpotQA), open-domain QA (NQ, TriviaQA), and tool/code (Gorilla APIBench API-call generation over HuggingFace/Torch Hub/TensorFlow Hub documentation).
baselines: LLaMA2-7B (0-shot prompting), LLaMA2-7B-chat + RAG, Domain-Specific Finetuning (DSF, 0-shot), DSF + RAG, and GPT-3.5 + RAG (provided as a stronger-model reference). Base model fine-tuned by RAFT is LLaMA2-7B.
key_metrics: Task accuracy / exact-match style scores per dataset (accuracy for PubMedQA/HotpotQA/NQ/TriviaQA; API-call correctness/accuracy for the Gorilla APIBench domains). No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are reported.
headline_result: RAFT (LLaMA2-7B) achieves 73.30 on PubMed, 35.28 on HotpotQA, 74.00 on HuggingFace, 84.95 on Torch Hub, and 86.86 on TensorFlow, consistently outperforming DSF, DSF+RAG, LLaMA2-7B+RAG, and even GPT-3.5+RAG (71.60/41.5/29.08/60.21/65.59). Gains over the base LLaMA-2 instruction-tuned model are as large as +35.25% on HotpotQA and +76.35% on Torch Hub; vs DSF, +30.87% on HotpotQA and +31.41% on HuggingFace.
ablations: (1) Effect of Chain-of-Thought (Table 2): RAFT with CoT vs without CoT yields +9.66% on HotpotQA (25.62 -> 35.28) and +14.93% on HuggingFace (59.07 -> 74.00), showing CoT with citations prevents overfitting and improves accuracy. (2) Fraction P% of training data containing the golden document (Sec 4.4, Fig 5 on NQ/TQA/HotpotQA): training with some examples lacking the golden context helps; optimal P% varies across datasets (around 40%/60%/100%), and overall ~80% golden inclusion is recommended (training setup: 1 golden + 4 distractors). (3) Number of distractor documents at train time and robustness to varying number of test-time documents (Sec 5, Fig 6 on NQ/TriviaQA/HotpotQA): training with distractors (best at D*+3D for NQ, D*+1D for HotpotQA) beats training with only golden documents and makes the model robust to varying test-time top-k.
evaluation_decoupling: No - Only end-to-end task metrics are reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are NOT reported separately because RAFT is retriever-agnostic and focuses on the reader.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final answer accuracy / API-call correctness). Reasoning/citation quality is examined qualitatively (Sec 4.3 case study showing RAFT cites correct source vs DSF error) and indirectly via the CoT ablation, but no quantitative process-level metric is reported.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Not a focus. Reported design choices have efficiency implications (a small LLaMA2-7B RAFT model matches/exceeds GPT-3.5+RAG, implying cost savings from using a smaller model), but explicit latency/token/cost numbers are not reported. CoT increases generation length. [uncertain] precise training compute and inference-cost numbers.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k. Training uses 1 golden + 4 distractor documents (k=5) per example; test-time evaluation typically uses top-3 retrieved documents. The Top-K generalization study (Sec 5) varies the number of train-time distractors and test-time documents but the default is a fixed small k.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A - Not a benchmark paper; it reuses existing datasets (PubMedQA, HotpotQA, NQ, TriviaQA, Gorilla APIBench). [uncertain] exact per-dataset training/eval sizes used in RAFT.
builds_on: Supervised fine-tuning / instruction tuning of LLMs (LLaMA-2); standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al. 2020); chain-of-thought reasoning; the Gorilla / APIBench line of work (Patil et al. 2023) for the code/API-call evaluation. Conceptually related to fine-tuning-for-RAG works (RA-DIT - Lin et al. 2023a, Atlas - Izacard et al. 2023, RETRO - Borgeaud et al. 2022).
contrasts_with: Standard RAG-on-a-general-model (no fine-tuning), domain-specific fine-tuning without context (DSF) and DSF+RAG, and prior fine-tuning-for-RAG methods (RA-DIT, etc.). Key contrast: prior fine-tuning-for-RAG works assume test-time domain/documents can differ from training; RAFT studies the opposite in-domain setting where train and test share the same document collection, and it explicitly trains with distractor documents (open-book-with-distractors) plus cite-then-reason CoT, unlike closed-book SFT or vanilla RAG.
lineage: Group B (RAG for task solving): a retrieval-augmented fine-tuning / training-recipe method that hardens the reader LLM for static-corpus, in-domain open-book RAG. Sits in the 'finetuning-for-RAG / noise-robust reader' lineage (alongside RA-DIT, Self-RAG) as opposed to experience/memory-based agent retrieval; emphasizes distractor robustness and cite-then-reason CoT over standard top-k RAG prompting.
